content:
Castle builds its relationship graph from the frontmatter of notes in `people/`.
This example library intentionally includes several shapes.

## What to look for

- **Relation colors:** the sample covers positive, neutral, flirty, mixed, and
  negative connections—from close collaborators to former coworkers.
- **Known-from branches:** expand Community, Work, Conference, University, and Family.
- **Organizations:** Northstar Labs has Research, Design, and Engineering departments;
  Harbor Commons has Programs and Partnerships.
- **Direct links:** dotted connections describe coworkers, friends, family, classmates,
  and manager relationships.
- **Map locations:** several people have coordinates; Jamie demonstrates multiple locations.

## Follow a cluster

Start with [Alex](/note/people/alex_morgan), follow the direct edge to
[Maya](/note/people/maya_singh), then open Maya's link to
[Sofia](/note/people/sofia_rossi). Their shared notes connect the people graph to the
broader knowledge graph through [Design principles](/note/notes/design_principles)
and the [Neighborhood Atlas](/note/projects/neighborhood_atlas/neighborhood_atlas).

occurrences.context: Then open Graph field guide and switch between relation and “known from” grouping.

| Explore | What it demonstrates | | --- | --- | | Graph field guide | Relationship colors, groups, departments, and direct links | | Neighborhood Atlas | A project connected to people, tasks, events, and research | | Why third places matter | A link-rich research note with citations and backlinks | | Field day journal | A dated narrative with an original field illustration | | Consent and care | A practical policy note with tasks, events, and follow-up links | | The stash | Quick captures for articles, videos, ideas, and loose follow-ups |
